# Speedle+

> Speedle+ is an open-source authorization engine for externalizing fine-grained access-control decisions across cloud-native and legacy applications.

Speedle+ evaluates RBAC and ABAC policies for users, services, and processes acting on behalf of users. Its human-readable Security Policy Definition Language (SPDL), centralized Policy Management Service, and Authorization Decision Service keep authorization logic outside application code. The project is available under the Universal Permissive License v1.0.

## Start here

- [Project overview](https://speedle.io/about/): What Speedle+ is and why the project exists.
- [Quick start](https://speedle.io/quick-start/): Run Speedle+ and make a first authorization decision.
- [Documentation](https://speedle.io/docs/): Concepts, deployment, APIs, and operations.
- [Architecture](https://speedle.io/docs/architecture/): Major components and request flow.
- [SPDL](https://speedle.io/docs/spdl/): Security Policy Definition Language reference.
- [Authorization decisions](https://speedle.io/docs/decisions/): How policy decisions are evaluated.
- [Use cases](https://speedle.io/docs/usecases/): Common authorization patterns.
- [Integrations](https://speedle.io/integrations/): Kubernetes, Istio, and Docker.
- [Source code](https://github.com/teramoby/speedle-plus): Canonical Speedle+ repository.

## Canonical facts

- Product name: Speedle+ (continuation of the original Speedle project)
- Category: open-source authorization engine / policy decision service
- Models: role-based access control (RBAC) and attribute-based access control (ABAC)
- Policy language: SPDL (Security Policy Definition Language)
- Core services: Policy Management Service and Authorization Decision Service
- License: Universal Permissive License v1.0
- Official website: https://speedle.io/
- Code repository: https://github.com/teramoby/speedle-plus

## Authorization and access control topics

- [Authorization and access control](https://speedle.io/docs/access-control/): How Speedle+ externalizes authorization decisions; RBAC, ABAC and PBAC can coexist.
- [Role-based access control (RBAC)](https://speedle.io/docs/access-control/rbac/): Role assignment, resource scope and role inheritance with executable SPDL policies.
- [Attribute-based access control (ABAC)](https://speedle.io/docs/access-control/abac/): Trusted attributes and typed policy conditions, with allow and deny examples.
- [Policy-based access control (PBAC)](https://speedle.io/docs/access-control/pbac/): Policy management, decision evaluation and application enforcement responsibilities.
- [Identity and access management (IAM)](https://speedle.io/docs/access-control/identity-iam/): Speedle's authorization role within IAM, identity domains and configured token assertion; not a complete identity provider.
- [Oracle Entitlements Server (OES)](https://speedle.io/docs/access-control/oes/): Architecture comparison and migration assessment; no drop-in compatibility claim.
- [XACML and SPDL](https://speedle.io/docs/access-control/xacml/): PAP/PDP/PEP correspondence and policy-language boundaries; no XACML conformance claim.
- [Playground](https://speedle.io/playground/): Evaluate SPDL policies locally using the real Go engine compiled to WebAssembly. No identity-provider or external-function calls.
